source_text: Sancti estote quia ego sanctus. Nomen sancti in scripturis non solum homines sed loca et vasa. Disce vim nominis ut opus impleas.
orientation: Origen is exhorting his hearers to holiness, explaining that the word 'holy' in Scripture applies not only to people but also to places and vessels.
pass_a_gloss: Holy [ones] be because I [am] holy. [The] name [of] holy [ones] in [the] scriptures [is] not only [for] men but [for] places and vessels. Learn [the] force [of the] name so that [the] work you may fulfill.

choices.english: Be holy because I am holy
choices.why: Direct command followed by the ground for the command; 'sanctus' rendered as 'holy' per glossary.
rejected: You shall be holy for I am holy

choices.why: Keeps the genitive 'sancti' as 'of holy' to preserve the idea that 'holy' is a name or title applied to things.
'Vis' here means the inherent power or meaning of the word; 'force' preserves the Latin sense of efficacy and meaning.

choices.english: so that you may fulfill the work
choices.why: Purpose clause with subjunctive; 'opus' is singular and refers to the work of holiness, not works generally.
rejected: so that you may do the work
in order to complete the work

pass_b_english: “Be holy because I am holy” (Leviticus 19:2). In the scriptures the name of holy is applied not only to men but also to places and vessels. Learn the force of the name so that you may fulfill the work.
